propositions: When two or more bundle objects exist for a single ref on S3, git ls-remote returns the ref at multiple SHAs and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable and causing push retries to stall indefinitely due to ambiguous ref resolution.

Upstream's interactive git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles blocks on input() prompts, crashes on EOF in non-interactive settings, and discards non-chosen heads to orphan refs without merging their events, causing data loss of unique ticket events that can never be recovered from an append-only log.

The heal must write a lossless merged tip bundle before deleting any original bundles and must never delete the merged tip itself, so that at every crash point at least one bundle carrying the full merged history remains remotely and mid-delete crashes re-heal to a single lossless bundle on the next run.

The heal acquires the helper's per-ref lock (IfNoneMatch conditional-put with 60s TTL and stale-lock steal), re-enumerates under the lock to guard against TOCTOU, and backs off without healing if another doctor wins the lock, allowing the backing-off process to converge on the winner's collapsed remote via its subsequent push retry.

The heal must fold N divergent bundle heads via iterated 2-parent lossless merges (not octopus merge), following sync's existing _union_merge semantics, reusing merge=ours for .bridge_state/* and handling unrelated-history heads via --allow-unrelated-histories, so every unique commit from every head remains reachable in the merged tip.

On a genuine non-derived-file conflict the heal must abort without deleting any remote bundle, release all locks, and surface rebar fsck-recover without silently discarding a parent, while push.py must invoke the heal exactly once per push call (guarded by healed_once flag) to prevent heal-retry thrash loops.
